name: stage-app
summary: A minimal Stage web application with a JSON endpoint, local run instructions and application checks. Add your first feature from here.
open_questions: What should the first useful feature do?

files.content:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Stage\Http\Application;
use Stage\Http\Response;
use Stage\Http\Route;

return new Application(
    Route::get('/', fn () => Response::json(['hello' => 'world'])),
);

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Stage\Http\Request;

require dirname(__DIR__) . '/vendor/autoload.php';

$app = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/app.php';
$response = $app->handle(new Request('GET', '/'));
if ($response->status !== 200 || json_decode($response->body, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR) !== ['hello' => 'world']) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Unexpected greeting response');
}
if ($app->handle(new Request('GET', '/missing'))->status !== 404) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Unknown paths must return 404');
}
echo "Greeting and missing-route checks passed\n";

# Stage application

A minimal PHP application with one JSON endpoint. Start here and add your first feature.

## Requirements

PHP 8.4 or a later PHP 8 release, Composer 2, and Git for version control.

## Run locally

In the extracted stage-app directory:

```sh
composer install
composer check
composer start
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 or run `curl http://127.0.0.1:8080` in a second terminal.
Expect `{"hello":"world"}`. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

`composer check` exercises the actual application: its greeting and a missing route.
This prepared starter was checked by the installation maintainer before release.
The chat does not execute visitor projects. Run these checks in your own environment,
and again after changes. PHP's built-in server is for local development only.

## Continue

Define routes in app.php. public/index.php is the web entry point. Only public/
should be exposed by a web server; vendor/, source, tests and project records stay
outside it. Keep the composer.lock created by Composer when you commit your work.

The included Git repository is on main with no commits, identity or remote.
`git status` shows your uncommitted files. Set your own identity and remote if needed.
No account, database, hosting, deployment or external integration is configured.

Stage documentation: https://stage.dev/resources/getting-started

# Current project

## Starting point

The Stage chat offers this minimal application before visitor-specific requirements
are known. PHP and Stage are the installation's default starting point, not a
confirmed requirement from the visitor. Another chosen language or platform replaces
this default.

## Implemented

- GET / returns the JSON object {"hello":"world"}
- Unrecognized routes return 404
- Local run and application checks are included

## Open decisions

What should the first useful feature do, and who will use it? No audience, data
storage, authentication, integrations or deployment choices have been assumed.
Continue the conversation to develop the project, or edit these files locally.
External edits are not synchronized back into the chat.
